name: The Stone Pine of the Bobolino
verify_notes: MASAF 14/D612/FI/09, girth 412 cm, height 31.5 m. Stands about 25 m from the live flo_007 and 45 m from flo_015, so it is the single cheapest addition left in Florence: a visitor already standing at the Bobolino cedars would not take a step. Held back only for want of a genuinely independent second source. The comune's list and the intoscana article that reports it both derive from the same MASAF designation, so they are one source repeated, not two. A RAMI per-tree page or the comune's own park inventory would settle it in one fetch.

name: The Monterey Cypress of the Giardino Simone Weil
verify_notes: MASAF 15/D612/FI/09, girth 388 cm, height 18.5 m, in a free public garden about 90 m from the Bobolino cluster. Same problem as the stone pine above: one register, no independent corroboration found in this pass. Monterey cypress is a striking species with a tiny native range on the California coast, so it would earn its place on the story alone if a second source turns up.

name: The Cypress of the Monte alle Croci Steps
verify_notes: MASAF 19/D612/FI/09, girth 346 cm, height 21.5 m. Sits on the stepped pilgrim climb from Piazza Poggi up to San Miniato al Monte, about 250 m from the live flo_009 ginkgo at Piazzale Michelangelo, so it would join the two hillside stops into a continuous route. Only the register and its municipal republication were found, which is one source. Worth one targeted search on the Via del Monte alle Croci scalinata before the next Florence pass.

name: The Aleppo Pine of Via Giramondino
verify_notes: MASAF 17/D612/FI/09, girth 323 cm, height 22.5 m, on Viale Galileo roughly midway between the Bobolino cluster and Piazzale Michelangelo. Would be the connecting stop on Poggi's Viale dei Colli walk. Single-sourced, and the smallest girth of the hillside candidates, so it is the weakest of the four on merit as well as on evidence.

name: The Strawberry Tree of the Giardino dell'Iris
verify_notes: MASAF 18/D612/FI/09, height 8.0 m, and the register records no girth at all. Stands about 40 m from the live flo_009 ginkgo, which is as tight as a pairing gets. Two problems, neither fatal: no girth and no age in any source found, and the Giardino dell'Iris opens only for a few weeks around the iris flowering each spring, so the access field would have to say so plainly and the season would effectively be the visit. A strawberry tree fruiting in autumn is a real best_time candidate if it ever clears the evidence bar.

name: The Chilean Wine Palm of Villa di Rusciano
verify_notes: MASAF 22/D612/FI/09, girth 349 cm, height 15.5 m. A genuinely uncommon species in Europe and a good story (the sap was tapped for palm honey until the species was nearly wiped out in Chile), in a municipal villa park. Failed on the count and on distance rather than on quality: it is about 1.6 km east of the Piazzale Michelangelo stop, so it does not join either existing walk. Keep for a third Florence walk if the east side is ever built out.

name: The Cypress of Villa della Petraia
verify_notes: MASAF 10/D612/FI/09, girth 580 cm, the second largest girth in the whole comune after the Montezuma cypress. Villa della Petraia is a Medici villa, a UNESCO site and open to the public, so access is fine. Failed purely on distance: 5 km north of the centre, joins no walk, and would repeat the scattering problem the live page already has. A strong candidate for a Medici villas collection rather than for the city page.

name: Further Orto Botanico trees on RAMI but not on MASAF
species: Acer x peronai, Ginkgo biloba, Liriodendron tulipifera
verify_notes: RAMI lists 6486 (hybrid maple), 6489 (ginkgo) and 6493 (tulip tree) inside the same garden, none of them on the national MASAF list. They would extend the tightest cluster on the site at zero walking cost. Not pursued this pass because the pass was scoped to the MASAF candidates and the count was already met, and because each needs its own second source. Note the site already has phenology files for ginkgo and tulip-tree, so both would render a year calendar immediately. This is the obvious next Florence job.
